subject.title: Codex native compaction discards topic diversity — agent misinterprets subsequent messages after topic switch

question: Should OpenClaw pursue an explicit Codex app-server contract for summary/retention metadata and then project bounded continuity context, or leave topic-retention quality entirely to native Codex compaction?
rationale: Current code intentionally prevents OpenClaw from replacing or rewriting native compaction, and the available lifecycle observations do not contain enough information to build a correctness-preserving topic index autonomously.

options.title: Sponsor a supported Codex continuity seam
options.body: Define or request an app-server summary/retention API or pre-turn projection contract, then implement bounded OpenClaw continuity only through that seam.

options.title: Keep native compaction opaque
options.body: Retain the current ownership boundary and close this request only if Codex-native behavior is shown to meet the continuity requirement without OpenClaw intervention.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a supported Codex continuity seam
recommendation.body: Define or request an app-server summary/retention API or pre-turn projection contract, then implement bounded OpenClaw continuity only through that seam.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work ties this person most directly to the native Codex compaction adapter and related compact/status paths.
